statement: Suppose $A+B+C=\\pi$. Show that $\\sin^{2}A+\\sin^{2}B+\\sin^{2}C=2+2\\cos A\\cos B\\cos C$.
solution: We use the companion identity valid for $A+B+C=\\pi$: $\\cos^{2}A+\\cos^{2}B+\\cos^{2}C+2\\cos A\\cos B\\cos C=1$ (which follows from writing $C=\\pi-A-B$ and simplifying). Then $\\sin^{2}A+\\sin^{2}B+\\sin^{2}C=3-(\\cos^{2}A+\\cos^{2}B+\\cos^{2}C)=3-(1-2\\cos A\\cos B\\cos C)=2+2\\cos A\\cos B\\cos C$.
